previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with advanced multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder with a suprapubic catheter, and a history of recurrent multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections, was admitted due to fever, lethargy, and septic shock. He was found to have a left distal femoral fracture managed non-operatively with a brace. Urine culture grew multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa, treated with piperacillin-tazobactam via a PICC line. He stabilized quickly, with resolution of sepsis and ongoing management of constipation, anemia, and pressure ulcers. His baclofen pump was refilled during admission. He was discharged to short-term rehab to complete antibiotics and receive supportive care, with follow-up planned in infectious disease and orthopedics.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Pressure ulcer of sacral region, stage 2
Other fracture of lower end of left femur, initial encounter for closed fracture
